questions.qtext:
Let $S=\{a, b\}$ be an alphabet, with total order $a<b$. Let $\Sigma=\text{S}^*$ be the set of all strings over $\text{S};$ for $w=s_1 s_2 \ldots s_n \in \Sigma$ we write $\ell(w)=n$, and for $1 \leqslant r \leqslant n=\ell(w)$ we write $w_r=s_1 s_2 \ldots s_r$. Denote by $\varepsilon$ the unique word of $\Sigma$ such that $\ell(\varepsilon)=0$, the null string. Conventionally $w_0=\varepsilon$ for all words $w \in \Sigma$.

Define relation $\prec$ on $\Sigma$ as follows:

Let $v, w \in \Sigma$, and $n=\min \{\ell(v), \ell(w)\}$. Let $r=\max \left\{i \mid v_i=w_i\right\} \leqslant n$.

Then $v \prec w$ if:
$$
\begin{array}{ccl}
\text { either } & (i) & \ell(v)=r \\
\text { or } & (i i) & v_{r+1}=v_r a, \quad w_{r+1}=w_r b, \quad \text { where } v_r=w_r .
\end{array}
$$

Which of the following is true for $(\Sigma,\prec)?$

options.text: $\prec$ is not reflexive and not symmetric.

\hline & \mathrm{d}=\operatorname{MAX}(\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}) \\
\hline \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B} & \\
\hline \mathrm{A}=\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B} & \\
\hline & \mathrm{A}=\mathrm{c} \\
\hline & \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{d} \\
\hline \text{Write} (\mathrm{A}) & \\
\hline & \text{Write} (\mathrm{A}) \\
\hline \text{Write} (\mathrm{B}) & \\
\hline & \text{Write(B)} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

questions.qtext:
In the context of the pipeline, 'Predict-not-taken' is a method of branch prediction in which the hardware assumes that the next instruction to be executed will be the instruction following the branch instruction in memory. This (possible) next instruction is placed in the pipe and execution begins. If after the branch is finished executing, it is found that we really wanted to take the branch, then the (possible) next instruction that we had been executing is thrown out by the hardware, and we begin executing the correct instruction, the branch target.
Consider two different $5$-stage pipeline machines $\text{(IF ID EX MEM WB).}$ The first machine $\mathrm{M}$ resolves branches in the $\mathrm{ID}$ stage, uses one branch delay slot, and can fill $80 \%$ of the delay slots with useful instructions. The second machine $\mathrm{N}$ resolves branches in the $\mathrm{EX}$ stage and uses a Predict-not-taken scheme.
Assume that the cycle times of the machines are identical. Given that $35 \%$ of the instructions are branches, $25 \%$ of branches are taken, and that stalls are due to branches alone, what is the Speedup of machine $\text{M}$ over machine $\mathrm{N}$ (up to three decimal places)? (Speedup is the ratio of machine $\mathrm{N}$ running time to machine $\mathrm{M}$ running time.)

}
